summary: This note traces the origins of the retailer Bed Bath & Beyond. Warren Eisenberg and Leonard Feinstein opened a store called Bed 'n Bath in Springfield, New Jersey in 1971, and by 1985 they ran 17 stores in the New York metropolitan area and California. That same year the company opened its first superstore to compete with rival linen retailers and renamed itself Bed Bath & Beyond to reflect the larger store size.
one_line: Origin story of Bed Bath & Beyond, from its 1971 Springfield, New Jersey store to its 1985 superstore and renaming.
key_facts: In 1971, Warren Eisenberg and Leonard Feinstein opened a store in Springfield, New Jersey called Bed 'n Bath.
By 1985, Warren Eisenberg and Leonard Feinstein were operating 17 stores in the New York metropolitan area and California.
In 1985, Bed Bath & Beyond opened its first superstore.
The first superstore was an attempt to remain competitive with Linens' n Things, Pacific Linen, and Luxury Linens.
Bed Bath & Beyond changed its name from Bed 'n Bath to represent the size increase in its retail stores.
The name change to Bed Bath & Beyond occurred in 1985, the same year the first superstore opened.
The company's original store was located in Springfield, New Jersey.
